title: 2015 AMC 12B Problem 18
statement: For every composite positive integer \(n,\) define \(r(n)\) to be the sum of the factors in the prime factorization of \(n.\) For example, \(r(50) = 12\) because the prime factorization of \(50\) is \(2 \cdot 5^2,\) and \(2 + 5 + 5 = 12.\) What is the range of the function \(r,\) \(\{r(n) : n \text{ is a composite positive integer}\}?\)

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: the set of composite positive integers

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: the set of even positive integers

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: the set of integers greater than \(3\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: the set of integers greater than \(4\)

solutions.text:
A composite number has at least two prime factors (with multiplicity), and the smallest prime is \(2,\) so the least possible value is \(2 + 2 = 4.\)

Every integer greater than \(3\) is attained: \(r(2^k) = 2k\) covers the even values \(\ge 4,\) and \(r(2^k\cdot 3) = 2k + 3\) covers the odd values \(\ge 5.\) So the range is the integers greater than \(3.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The smallest value comes from the smallest composite, \(4 = 2 \cdot 2\)
Show every integer greater than \(3\) is attained, e.g. \(r(2^k) = 2k\) and \(r(2^k\cdot 3) = 2k + 3\)
